speaker: Doctor
text:
I see you have frequent epistaxis, mucous membrane bleeding, and petechiae. To understand the cause, how old are you, and do you have a history of easy bruising or excessive bleeding after minor injuries?

Also, do you take any medications, and has anyone in your family ever had bleeding problems or been told they had a clotting disorder?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (ITP). Given the child's age and presentation with isolated mucosal bleeding, petechiae, and easy bruising without a family history of clotting disorders, ITP is the most likely etiology.
